alex: quick heads-up — ran a focused microbench on the packed-kernel path + paged KV cache for seq=1024 and saw a regression vs baseline flash variant. not huge but reproducible on g5.

sara: can you drop the numbers and command?

jamal: ran: `./bench_attn --model=gpt2 --seq=1024 --bs=4 --repeat=50 --kernels=pkg_paged,flash_alt`

jamal: output snippet:
```
pkg_paged: mean=31.8ms p50=31.1 p95=36.4
flash_alt: mean=29.2ms p50=28.9 p95=33.0
mem: pkg_paged resident ~4.8GB, flash_alt ~5.3GB
```

ci-bot: PERF ALERT: throughput regressed 8.7% on bench/attn/1024 (build: ci/4728). See: https://ci.redwood/c/4728/bench-logs

lia: interesting that mem is slightly lower for pkg_paged but latency higher. could be scheduling / more kernel launches due to page fault handling + small batch effects. did you warm the KV pages?

jamal: warmed KV by running a prefix pass; confirmed behavior persists. also tried bs=8 and bs=1 — relative gap shrinks at bs=8, widens at bs=1.

mike: hypothesis: QKV packing changed memory alignment so epilogue (softmax+out) sees extra memcpy/strides on paged layout. also possible bank contention on the smaller working set.

alex: @mike @lia want a quick triage checklist: 1) reproduce with nvprof/cupti, 2) collect kernel timeline, 3) check kernel chooser heuristics (we might be picking a fallback path for certain seq/chunk sizes), 4) try epilogue-fused variant without packing.

lia: wrote a small heuristic tweak to chooser: if seq>=512 and bs<=4 and paged_kv_enabled: prefer flash_alt unless packed gives >=3% improvement in 95p in last window. pseudocode: 
```
if seq >= 512 and batch <= 4 and paged_kv:
    choose = flash_alt
else:
    choose = packed_paged
```

mike: I'll try a targeted build: disable pack alignment optimization and run the same bench. if latency drops, we know where to look. also test epilogue fusion by linking `-DFUSE_EPILOGUE=1` build.

jamal: dropping results here after runs. cc @alex

[--- end of thread ---]
